rites.name: Telaustisia
rites.text: Telaustisia is a concept in Kelordaren: the doctrine that a grove's growth can be bound into a lasting oath between kingdoms. In the Courts it was invoked when the first sovereign's councils sealed the early doors between worlds. Its power is measured in the small, patient works of rooted things rather than in cataclysm.

rites.name: Tenvamtaala
rites.text: Tenvamtaala is a concept in Kelordaren, a notion of the sustained vigil kept by the Courts during the Holy Age, when flame-tended temples and sworn orders watched over the doors between worlds. It names the discipline of holding a single flame steady through a full night of council deliberation.

rites.name: Zephiavsora
rites.text: Zephiavsora is a concept in the Kelordaren universe, a quiet pattern of thread-light that the makers weave into the ground during the Seeding. Its power sleeps beneath the soil, waking only as a faint hum when the Weave takes root.

rites.name: Brarnusteld
rites.text: Brarnusteld is a concept of the Kelordaren omniverse, a binding principle that the makers set into the Weave during the Seeding. It describes how small, patient powers were first allowed to sleep within the growing groves of the first sovereign's age.

rites.name: Zephashis
rites.text: Zephashis is a concept of the Kelordaren, a binding of wind and root that the first sovereign used to keep the groves standing as the Fall split the land. It was sworn into the Pact during the Sundering, when the Shards were still settling into their new shapes. Its lasting role was to steady growing kingdoms against the storms that followed.

rites.name: Kraithurn
rites.text: Kraithurn is the concept of a binding oath that holds the fractured landmasses of Kelordaren together during the Age of Sundering. It is spoken of as the force that let broken shores remember their old kinship. Its strength lies in persuading severed lands to keep their promises rather than in any single blow.

rites.name: Zephethizis
rites.text: Zephethizis is a concept within Kelordaren, a notion of the Three Futures where the ending branches and the Library shelves each outcome. It arose in the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke old bonds between the people of the shore towns. Its power is modest, measured in the scale of a single household or a small workshop.
